summary.title: A New Organocatalytic Desymmetrization Reaction Enables the Enantioselective Total Synthesis of Madangamine E
summary.authors: Shinya Shiomi; Benjamin D A Shennan; Ken Yamazaki; Ángel L Fuentes De Arriba; Dhananjayan Vasu; Trevor A Hamlin; Darren J Dixon
summary.executive_summary: This paper reports the first enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E, a complex marine alkaloid, achieved in 30 steps. The strategy centers on a novel, highly efficient organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction: an intramolecular Michael addition of a prochiral ketone to a tethered β,β'-disubstituted nitroolefin. This key step constructs the chiral bicyclic ABC core in near-perfect enantio- and diastereoselectivity, establishing three stereocenters including a quaternary carbon. The reaction's mechanism was elucidated using DFT calculations, revealing a cooperative push/pull mechanism stabilized by hydrogen bonding. Following core construction, the synthesis proceeded via oxidative lactamization, Z-selective olefination of a hindered ketone, and two ring-closing metathesis (RCM) reactions to close the macrocyclic rings. The work demonstrates the power of catalytic desymmetrization for generating stereochemical complexity from simple achiral precursors.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper reports the first enantioselective total synthesis of madangamine E, a complex marine alkaloid, achieved in 30 steps. The strategy centers on a novel, highly efficient organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction: an intramolecular Michael addition of a prochiral ketone to a tethered β,β'-disubstituted nitroolefin. This key step constructs the chiral bicyclic ABC core in near-perfect enantio- and diastereoselectivity, establishing three stereocenters including a quaternary carbon. The reaction's mechanism was elucidated using DFT calculations, revealing a cooperative push/pull mechanism stabilized by hydrogen bonding. Following core construction, the synthesis proceeded via oxidative lactamization, Z-selective olefination of a hindered ketone, and two ring-closing metathesis (RCM) reactions to close the macrocyclic rings. The work demonstrates the power of catalytic desymmetrization for generating stereochemical complexity from simple achiral precursors.

Research Context
The madangamine family features a complex pentacyclic fused-ring system. Only two total syntheses and one formal synthesis of madangamine A exist. Previous strategies relied on stereoselective cyclocondensation or N-acyl-iminium cyclization. There is a need for efficient routes to generate structural complexity. Desymmetrization reactions could install stereochemical information from a single step.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can a catalytic desymmetrization reaction construct the madangamine core? Will an intramolecular Michael addition establish a quaternary center? Can DFT rationalize the enantioselectivity of this new reaction? Can the full molecule be synthesized from this core? The reaction will exhibit high enantio- and diastereoselectivity.

Methodological Details
The study utilized a 30-step synthetic route to madangamine E. A model substrate, methyl-substituted nitroolefin 7, was developed. The model was synthesized in 3 steps from 1,4-cyclohexanedione monoethylene acetal. Catalysts tested included trans-cyclohexanediamine and proline-derived scaffolds. Reactions were run in dichloromethane with 20 mol% catalyst loading. Benzoic acid was used as a co-catalyst. Stereochemistry was confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. The target nitroolefin 17 was synthesized on a 17 g scale. The key cyclization was performed on a >5 g scale. Ketone 3 was elaborated using organocerium and organozinc reagents.

Procedures And Architectures
The key step is an intramolecular Michael addition of a ketone to a nitroolefin. Jacobsen's thiourea catalyst 9f was identified as the optimal catalyst. The reaction proceeds via a hemiaminal intermediate Int1. An imine Int2 forms after water elimination. Enamine Int3 is formed by tautomerization from imine Int2. The transition structure TS1 is stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The mechanism is described as a cooperative push/pull-type mechanism. The nitroolefin 17 was accessed via selenoxide elimination. Oxidative lactamization used AZADO, copper chloride, and DMAP. Z-selective olefination used SOCl2 and DTBMP. RCM of the D ring used Grubbs 1st generation catalyst. RCM of the E ring used Hoveyda-Grubbs 2nd generation catalyst. The final step was a double amide reduction with LiAlH4.

Key Results
The model reaction gave product 8 in 70% yield. The model reaction achieved 99% ee as a single diastereomer. The simplified catalyst 9e gave 51% yield and 96% ee. DFT calculated a ΔΔG‡ of 3.0 kcal mol⁻¹ favoring TS1. DFT predicted 99% ee, matching experimental results. The reaction is highly exergonic with ΔGrxn = -19.4 kcal mol⁻¹. Nitroolefin 17 was synthesized in 52% yield over 3 steps. The key cyclization of 17 gave product 18 in 95% yield. The cyclization achieved >99% ee on a >5 g scale. Ketone homologation and epoxide opening gave aldehyde 23 in 86% yield. Boc-deprotection and reductive amination gave aminodiol 4 in 79% yield. Oxidative lactamization afforded tricyclic enone 25 in good yield. RCM of 25 gave tetracyclic enone 26 in 82% yield. Z-selective olefination gave skipped diene 28 in 90% yield. RCM of 29 gave diamide 30 in 71% yield. Final reduction afforded synthetic madangamine E in 72% yield.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The reaction establishes three stereocenters including a quaternary carbon. The transition structure benefits from hydrogen bonding interactions. The mechanism involves thiourea, nitro group, and enamine moieties. The C-C bond formation is irreversible and stereoselectivity-determining. The pKa difference drives the protonation preference. The strategy enables rapid generation of stereochemical complexity. The method applies to high-value saturated molecular scaffolds.

Contradictions And Limitations
Previous Wittig approaches on ketone 3 were largely unsuccessful. Ketone 3 is sensitive to competing deprotonation pathways. RCM of the E ring initially failed due to spatial arrangement. The organocerium reaction was highly capricious. Supporting Information is required for detailed procedures.

Claims
The new organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction enables the total synthesis of madangamine E. 30-step enantioselective total synthesis was achieved. Bicyclic core constructed with near-perfect selectivity. Three stereocenters including a quaternary carbon established. Previous strategies required more complex core construction. Demonstrates utility of catalytic desymmetrization in natural product synthesis.
DFT calculations successfully rationalize the enantioselectivity of the key cyclization. Computed 99% ee matches experimental 99% ee. Transition structure TS1 is energetically favorable. Hydrogen bonding stabilizes the preferred transition state. Other transition structures were less favorable. Provides mechanistic insight into substrate/catalyst interactions.

Data And Code Availability
Detailed procedures are in the Supporting Information. Computational methods are described in the Supporting Information.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Catalyst 9f was uniquely efficient compared to others. Simplified catalyst 9e also worked well. Reaction conditions were optimized for scalability. RCM conditions were optimized to minimize isomerization.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1A shows the pentacyclic fused-ring system of madangamines. Figure 1B shows previous total syntheses of madangamines. Figure 1C shows the retrosynthetic analysis of madangamine E. Figure 2A shows inspiration from previous desymmetrization work. Figure 2B shows catalysts tested and the catalytic cycle. Figure 2C shows the DFT-computed reaction pathway.

Three Takeaways
1. A new organocatalytic desymmetrization reaction enables total synthesis. 2. DFT rationalizes the mechanism with 99% ee prediction. 3. The strategy allows rapid generation of stereochemical complexity.
